case.case_title: Ekanayake v. Gunatilleke, Superintendent of Police, Maho and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 1007/92, decided on 24 September 1993

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s detention without a valid detention order and prolonged custody violated Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was detained without being served a detention order and was held in custody for over 80 days without lawful justification.
key_facts: Petitioner was detained at Maho police station on orders of the 1st respondent without being shown a detention order.
Petitioner was produced before the Magistrate after 30 days but was returned to police custody.
Petitioner was detained until 19.11.92 and then released unconditionally.
No valid detention order was produced to justify the initial or continued detention.
No charges were filed against the petitioner during detention.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any detained person be brought before a judge and that detention must be supported by a valid legal order. The court found that the petitioner’s detention without a valid detention order and prolonged custody without lawful justification violated this constitutional protection.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the petitioner was detained without being served a detention order and was held in custody for over 80 days without lawful justification or charges, the court held that his detention violated Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention without a valid detention order is unconstitutional under Article 13(2).
Prolonged detention without judicial authorization or charges violates constitutional rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s detention violated Article 13(2) of the Constitution.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner’s detention was unlawful because it was not supported by a valid detention order and he was held without judicial authorization.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was detained without being shown a detention order and was held in custody for over 80 days without charges or lawful justification.
